author: Zhané Caldwell
title: Bronx fire displaces families, injures 12 including children - NewsBreak
text:
By Zhané Caldwell ,
1 hours ago
FORDHAM, The Bronx (PIX11) — Twelve people are hospitalized following a fire in the Bronx that displaced at least two families, according to officials.
According to the FDNY, the dozen people hospitalized include children and adults.
Trapped child rescued from Bronx apartment fire, video shows Citizen app video showed a man carrying a child while standing on top of scaffolding, and two men smashing the glass of an apartment window in a desperate attempt to help as heavy smoke poured from a building near Ryer Avenue and East 181st Street.
Deputy Chief Andrew Holzmaier said the fire broke out around 4:00 Wednesday on the third floor of the building, where firefighters faced challenges inside.
“There was a clutter condition within the apartment which made the searches a little difficult but overall, we were able to overcome them,” he said.
Part of the building now stands charred with shattered windows. According to the FDNY, 12 people were taken to nearby hospitals — one in critical condition and two with serious but non-life-threatening injuries. Maria Lascano described her experience trying to escape the building.
“My dad, he has issues with his legs,” said Lascano. “I couldn’t bring him down ‘cause I was bringing down my youngest son. We did inhale a lot of smoke so, we came down fast and I had to tell the fireman — I was like please help me ‘cause my father was sitting on the fourth floor. He couldn’t come down.”
The Red Cross said it has registered five apartments for assistance, with families in at least two of them displaced. The fire was mainly contained to one unit, but smoke and water damage are impacting surrounding apartments, according to fire officials. Businesses below the mixed-use building were also impacted. Milka Beauty Salon is without electricity, and The Alamo deli is facing a major cleanup after water leaked through the ceiling, forcing it to close.
“We might need a couple of days to recover, sanitize, change the place, maintain the store again to come back and continue work,” said Sadam Al-Adwar, who manages the deli.
Assemblymember Yudelka Tapia said she’s working to help impacted residents in addition to the support they’re getting from the Red Cross.
“My office is going to get in charge of whatever they need aside from that,” Tapia said.
No deaths have been reported. The cause of the fire is under investigation.
